response.sql:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, c.gender, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
  FROM Customers AS c
  LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.gender
), shares AS (
  SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count,
         1.0 * order_count / SUM(order_count) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) AS share
  FROM customer_orders
), above_average AS (
  SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count, share,
         share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_above_average
  FROM shares
)
SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count, share, share_above_average
FROM above_average
WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM shares)
ORDER BY share_above_average DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The average share is the unweighted arithmetic mean of each gender-recorded customer's share, including customers with zero orders; shares use all orders placed by gender-recorded customers as the denominator for that gender.
